planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container vines in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis or arbor in full sun; Janet is a pistillate (female-flowered) cultivar and needs a self-fertile muscadine such as Carlos or Nesbitt within about 50 feet for reliable pollination.

directions: Janet is a large, bronze-skinned muscadine released by Ison's Nursery in 1988 and named for Bill and Leola Ison's daughter, Janet Ison McClure. It is regarded as one of the more cold-hardy bronze female varieties and ripens late with an uneven, extended harvest window, so expect to pick over several weeks rather than all at once. The berries have a persistently wet stem scar that tears on picking, which keeps Janet out of commercial fresh-market packing lines but is a non-issue for home gardeners eating fruit straight off the vine or pressing it for juice. Because it is female-flowered rather than self-fertile, plant it alongside a perfect-flowered cultivar to ensure good fruit set.
sources: University of Georgia Muscadine Grape Breeding Program

planting.note: Plant dormant cuttings or container vines in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis or arbor in full sun; self-fertile, so a single vine will set fruit without a separate pollinizer.

directions: Mighty Fine (selection AM-70) was released in fall 2025 by the University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture's fruit breeding program, named for retired breeder John Clark's favorite phrase of approval. It is a self-fertile, black-skinned muscadine with notably large berries bred for fresh eating, and it carries better cold tolerance than most Southern-bred muscadines, extending the crop's range further north than older varieties like Carlos or Noble. In 2022 field-day taste trials it beat out the long-standard Supreme cultivar as attendees' favorite fresh-eating muscadine. Give it full sun and a sturdy trellis; as a very new release, long-term disease performance outside Arkansas trial plots is still being documented.
sources: University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture

planting.note: Plant dormant cuttings or container vines in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis in full sun; plant near a self-fertile muscadine cultivar to ensure good pollination, since Altus's flower type has not been widely documented outside university trial plots.

directions: Altus (selection AM-77) was released alongside Mighty Fine in fall 2025 by the University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture, co-developed by enologist Renee Threlfall specifically for wine and juice production rather than fresh eating. It is a smaller-berried, black-skinned, seeded muscadine, and in consumer trials the pressed juice outscored the long-standard wine cultivar Noble for flavor, sourness balance, and overall impression. Like Mighty Fine, it was bred with an emphasis on cold hardiness that should let growers push muscadine culture into cooler zones than traditional Gulf South and Deep South selections tolerate. Being a brand-new release, expect limited nursery availability and thin long-term field data for the next few seasons.
sources: University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture
